segments.text: Jay runs into Cameron while having lunch with some old friends. Instead of introducing him as Mitchell’s partner, Jay calls him “a friend of my son.” Cameron lets it go, but Mitchell doesn’t.

segments.text: He and Cam have been together for five years and are raising Lily, so Mitchell is tired of Jay acting like their relationship is something he has to hide from other people.

segments.text: When Mitchell confronts him, Jay says his old friends wouldn’t understand. Mitchell decides to mess with him and claims that Jay’s friend Shorty is gay. He isn’t, but Mitchell sounds so sure that Jay starts wondering if he’s missed something obvious for thirty years.

segments.text: Gloria makes it worse by saying she believes it too. She pushes Jay to talk to Shorty because Jay has a gay son and should know how to handle it. So Jay takes Shorty to the driving range and awkwardly tells him that whatever secret he’s carrying, he can open up.

segments.text: Shorty finally admits the truth: he owes a dangerous bookie twenty thousand dollars. Jay, still thinking they’re talking about being gay, has basically offered to help before he understands what the secret is.

segments.text: Jay is furious when he finds out Mitchell made the whole thing up. Mitchell apologizes, but he’s also genuinely proud of his father. Jay was uncomfortable, but he still tried to support a friend he thought was gay. That’s more progress than Mitchell expected.

segments.text: Meanwhile, Phil installs a complicated universal remote and Claire can’t get it to work. Phil keeps explaining it in the kind of patient voice that makes her want to throw something, so she finally does—she breaks the remote.

segments.text: Phil buys the same one again and makes a bet: he can teach Haley to use it in twenty minutes. Claire is sure he’ll fail, but Haley learns it. Claire admits he proved his point, then quietly wakes Haley later that night and asks her to teach her instead. She’s willing to learn.

segments.text: At Jay and Gloria’s house, Manny is expecting a date with Whitney, a girl he met in an online book club. The problem is that Whitney is a grown woman who thought Manny was an adult too. The date dies immediately, but Gloria feels sorry for her and gives her a makeover.

segments.text: Later, Whitney meets Cameron, and the two instantly connect over clothes, old movies, and vampire books. Whitney leaves convinced she may have met the perfect man, without realizing Cameron is gay.

segments.text: Nobody becomes a different person. Jay gets a little more open-minded, Claire learns the remote, and Whitney gets some confidence back. Maybe fifteen percent really is enough.
